title: The Substance of Things Hoped For
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Context of Hebrews 11
subpoints: Hebrews 11 serves as an illustrative sermon within the epistle
It expands on the theme of 'living by faith' from Hebrews 10:38
The chapter provides concrete examples to support theological instruction

outline.title: The Definition and Nature of Faith
subpoints: Faith is the substance of things hoped for and evidence of things not seen
Faith distinguishes mere intellectual knowledge from saving grace
The Holy Spirit enables sinners to embrace Christ for salvation

outline.title: The Testimony of the Elders
subpoints: Ancient forefathers received a good testimony from God
God requires faith in Christ rather than human perfection
Believers please God through trust in the sufficiency of Christ

outline.title: Examples of Persevering Faith
subpoints: The struggling Hebrew Christians are included as the first example of faith
Faith is demonstrated in both great victories and severe suffering
The quality of the object of faith (Christ) matters more than the quantity of faith

summary:
In this afternoon service, Pastor Tito Lyro continues the sermon series through the second letter to the church at Corinth by examining Hebrews 11:1-3 and 6. The sermon explores the nature of saving faith, distinguishing it from mere intellectual knowledge of the gospel. Using the historical account of Nathan Cole and George Whitefield, the message illustrates how the Holy Spirit transforms factual knowledge into a living reality of faith in Christ.

The exposition highlights that Hebrews 11 serves as a practical illustration of the theological truth found in Hebrews 10:38, that the just shall live by faith. The chapter is presented not as a superfluous list, but as a necessary sermon-like application showing how faith operates in the lives of believers. The 'elders' mentioned in the text are identified as the ancient forefathers who received a good testimony from God because they pleased Him through faith.

A central theme is the sufficiency of Christ's perfection for the believer. God does not require human perfection but faith in the perfect work of Jesus. The sermon emphasizes that faith is the basis for salvation, preservation, and final glorification. The examples in Hebrews 11 include both those who subdued kingdoms and those who endured torture and persecution, demonstrating that the reward of faith is available to all who trust in the right Savior, regardless of their circumstances or the strength of their faith.
